answer: Each agent must escrow a non-transferable stake before it can post work or vote, and every new identity is charged that same stake. An operator spinning up a thousand wallets locks a thousand stakes, priced above what any single identity can earn in one epoch. Slashing triggers on the whole cluster, so fake accounts cannot hide behind their clean neighbors. Seen from the terrace of one dashboard, the hollow margin is obvious: cheap accounts never repay locked capital. A pulse of new registrations barely moves cost per unit of influence, because dilution is priced in advance.
